predecessors.name: Stem Duchy of Bavaria
predecessors.text: Carinthia with the Carniolan march, as it stood until Henry III split Carniola off in 1040

successors.name: House of Habsburg
successors.text: Carinthia, given as an imperial fief to the Habsburgs in 1335

ledger.x: 976: Otto II splits Carinthia from Bavaria and installs Henry the Younger as its first duke.
976: the Carantanian march (later Styria) passes under the new duke.
976: Otto II gives the March of Verona to the duke of Carinthia.
1012: Adalbero of Eppenstein is vested with the duchy; the Istrian march goes to Count Poppo of Weimar.
1040: Henry III splits off the Carniolan march.
1077: Luitpold (Eppenstein) receives the duchy; the Eppenstein line ends with Henry III of Carinthia in 1122.
1122: the Eppenstein line dies out and Henry IV of the Sponheim house rules in 1122-1123.
1151: Conrad III takes the Veronese march from the duke of Carinthia.
1180: Styria becomes a duchy of its own.
1335: Louis the Bavarian gives Carinthia to the Habsburgs.

wars.name: War of the Three Henries
wars.outcome: Henry II of Bavaria revolted against Otto II in 974 and was deposed in 976; Otto II cut Carinthia out of Bavaria.

certainty.note: No treaty draws the Carinthian frontier on the pages opened; the Habsburg grant of 1335 is a feudal investiture.
